In 1991 I was in high school and was involved with the school band.  Three schools from my city in Ontario, Canada travelled to Boston to participate in the Kiwanis Music Festival.  On our second day in Boston, 4 students between  the 3 Canadian schools got sick and were taken to a local hospital. It didn’t take the nurses and doctors in the ER very long to determine that the students had the measles. An official from the health department was immediately notified and contacted our teachers notifying us that we were being quarantined at our hotel, and forbidden from leaving our rooms. He also announced we were being deported from the state early the following morning. gave us specific instructions that until we crossed the Massachusetts state line, we weren’t allowed to stop or get off the buses.  Between the 3 Ontario Canada schools, we turned 1 bus into a quarantine bus (by the time we departed, 8 of our students were on the quarantine bus), and the rest of us crammed together with our rivals into the remaining 2 buses back to Canada. When we got home,  an active measles outbreak had started that lasted for about 9 months. And it turns out that the officials in Boston acted so quickly that while other places in the US suffered from the same outbreak, Boston only had intermittent cases… 
I can officially say that I’ve been band in the USA ( get it, band… You know, cause I was there with the high school band… I digress)!
